soste.title: Louis XIV's forts guard the port
Rue Imperiale cuts through the old town

cards.title: A colony on the Lacydon
lines: Greeks from Phocaea, in Asia Minor, found Massalia around 600 BC.
The settlers choose the hills north of a sheltered inlet, the Lacydon.

cards.title: A second wave
lines: After the Persians destroy Phocaea, new colonists arrive around 540 BC.

cards.title: Walls of limestone and clay
lines: A first rampart rises in the late 5th century BC.
It is rebuilt in the 4th century and on a large scale in the 2nd.

cards.title: Pytheas sails north
lines: The Massaliote navigator Pytheas explores the Atlantic coasts, around 330-320 BC.

cards.title: Rome comes to the rescue
lines: Gallic tribes threaten the city in 123-121 BC; Roman armies drive them back.
The alliance with Rome grows closer.

cards.title: A city that backed the wrong side
lines: After Caesar's siege the city keeps nominal autonomy but loses its trading empire.

cards.title: Christians in the Roman port
lines: Christianity appears in Roman Massilia; catacombs above the harbor mark an early community.

cards.title: The martyr Victor
lines: Around 290 Victor is martyred in Marseille; the abbey of Saint-Victor will take his name.

cards.title: Cassian and Saint-Victor
lines: Tradition says the monk John Cassian founds two monasteries at Saint-Victor around 415.
Archaeology finds nothing there before the late 5th century.

cards.title: The Goths arrive
lines: Visigoth forces under King Euric take Marseille around 470.
Franks follow in 536 (some sources say 537).

cards.title: Charles Martel sacks the city
lines: Arab forces invited into Provence are driven out in 739 as the Franks sack Marseille.

cards.title: Raiders from the sea
lines: Saracens sack Marseille in 839.

cards.title: Three lords, one city
lines: In feudal times the city is split between the bishop, the viscount and the abbey of Saint-Victor.

cards.title: A commune and a chapel
lines: Marseille governs itself as a commune from the early 13th century (sources differ: 1212-18).
In 1214 a priest begins a chapel on the Garde hill.

cards.title: Anjou takes Marseille
lines: Charles of Anjou, count of Provence since 1246, takes the city in 1252.
A revolt is crushed in 1262-63.

cards.title: The Black Death
lines: Plague kills about 15,000 of 25,000 inhabitants.

cards.title: The Aragonese sack the port
lines: Alfonso V of Aragon sacks the city on 20 November 1423.

cards.title: Provence joins France
lines: Charles III dies in December 1481 and leaves Provence to Louis XI.
The union is confirmed in 1486.

cards.title: A siege lifted
lines: Imperial troops besiege the city in August-September 1524.
They withdraw as Francis I marches to its relief.

cards.title: The king enters through a breach
lines: Louis XIV subdues a rebellious Marseille in 1660.
Forts Saint-Jean and Saint-Nicolas are built to watch the city.

cards.title: A new city beyond the walls
lines: In 1666 the king decides to enlarge Marseille; the old ramparts are razed in 1672 and a new wall follows in 1694.
A galley arsenal fills the port from 1665.

cards.title: The Great Plague
lines: A ship from the Levant brings plague in 1720.
About 38,000 of 75,000 inhabitants die.

cards.title: The song of the Marseillais
lines: Volunteers march from Marseille to Paris in 1792; their song becomes La Marseillaise.

cards.title: The city without a name
lines: After a federalist revolt, Marseille is renamed Ville-sans-nom in 1793.

cards.title: A new port for steam
lines: The Joliette basin is authorized in 1844 and completed in 1853.
The Old Port is no longer enough.

cards.title: Water for a growing city
lines: The Canal de Marseille opens in 1849.

cards.title: The Docks of the Joliette
lines: Giant warehouses rise from 1858; completion dates range from 1863 to 1866.
The Arenc basin was begun in November 1856.

cards.title: Suez opens
lines: The Suez Canal opens in 1869 and boosts the port; the Palais Longchamp is completed the same year.

cards.title: A street changes its name
lines: On 16 October 1870 the Rue Imperiale becomes the Rue de la Republique.

cards.title: Horse-drawn trams
lines: Horse-drawn trams begin to run in 1876.

cards.title: Cholera
lines: A cholera epidemic strikes the city in 1884.

cards.title: 2,500 years
lines: Marseille celebrates the 2,500th anniversary of its founding in 1899.
Olympique de Marseille is formed the same year.

cards.title: Plague returns
lines: Bubonic plague breaks out again in September 1903.

cards.title: The colonial exhibition
lines: Marseille hosts colonial exhibitions in 1906 and 1922.

cards.title: The Grand Theatre burns
lines: The Grand Theatre burns down on 13 November 1919.

cards.title: An airport and a second exhibition
lines: Marseille Provence Airport opens in 1922, the year of a second colonial exhibition.

cards.title: Assassination on the quay
lines: King Alexander I of Yugoslavia and French minister Louis Barthou are assassinated on 9 October 1934.

cards.title: A stadium for the city
lines: The Stade Velodrome opens in 1937.

cards.title: Vichy and the bombs
lines: In June 1940 German and Italian aircraft bomb Marseille.
The city then lies in the unoccupied zone, under the Vichy regime.

cards.title: German troops occupy the city
lines: In November 1942 German forces occupy Marseille.

cards.title: The Saint-Jean quarter is gone
lines: On 22-24 January 1943 a police roundup arrests more than 6,000 people and expels about 20,000.
From 1 February about 1,500 buildings on 14 hectares are dynamited.

cards.title: Liberation
lines: Marseille is liberated in late August 1944.
The Germans blow up the Transporter Bridge on 22 August.

cards.title: Rebuilding the Old Port
lines: From 1949 the architect Fernand Pouillon builds new stone blocks on both sides of the Hotel de Ville.
The district is finished by 1956; the old lanes do not return.

cards.title: Le Corbusier's Radiant City
lines: The Cite Radieuse is inaugurated on 14 October 1952: a 56-meter slab of apartments after five years of work.

cards.title: The pieds-noirs
lines: After Algerian independence in 1962 about 150,000 pieds-noirs settle in Marseille.

cards.title: A tunnel under the Old Port
lines: The Old Port tunnel opens in 1967.

cards.title: Metro and a shipping giant
lines: The first metro line opens in 1977.
The shipping company CMA CGM is founded the same year.

cards.title: The TGV arrives
lines: The TGV Sud-Est begins serving Marseille in 1983.

cards.title: Euromediterranee
lines: In 1995 the state and the city launch Euromediterranee: 310 hectares around La Joliette.
An extension adds 170 hectares from 2007.

cards.title: 2,600 years
lines: The Parc du 26e Centenaire opens in 2001, marking 2,600 years since the founding.

cards.title: Tramway and a bigger waterfront
lines: The first tramway line opens in 2007.
Euromediterranee adds 170 hectares to the north.

cards.title: A tower for a shipping giant
lines: Zaha Hadid's 147-meter CMA CGM Tower is completed in September 2011.
